summary: Joseph Mosseri explains the traditional community practice for the all-night reading of Shavuot, known as Tiqun Lel Shavuot. He details the order of reading from Torah, Nevi'im, Ketuvim, and the Idra Rabbah of the Zohar, and discusses the tradition regarding the timing of the morning prayers at sunrise.
questions: What is the traditional order of reading for the night of Shavuot?
Which rabbis and communities followed the traditional Shavuot all-night reading?
When should prayers begin on the morning of Shavuot?
What did Hacham Chaim Tawil write about the timing of prayers on Shavuot morning?
